cover.headline: The anchor biologics contract has gone and the market has priced Syngene as if growth went with it: on its own forward EV/EBITDA history and the pharma sector's move the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}}, a BUY, with a DCF that says the recovery must be real
cover.lead: Syngene International (52.4% owned by Biocon) does contract research for drug makers (research services: discovery, dedicated centres such as BMS's 700-scientist unit, translational and clinical work; ~65% of FY26 revenue of ₹3,739 cr) and develops and manufactures their drugs (CDMO, small and large molecules; ~35%). Its biologics plants were built around one commercial product, Zoetis's Librela, under a 10-year programme worth up to US$500 mn; Librela orders collapsed in FY26 and were close to zero in Q1FY27, when revenue fell 16% and the margin fell to 12%. A new Biocon-bred team (Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw as executive chair, Siddharth Mittal as CEO) calls FY27 a 'transition year' and promises growth from FY28. We forecast EPS of ₹5.2 / 8.6 / 11.3 for FY27-29E. The brokers that disclose a method use **EV/EBITDA**, and so do we: Syngene's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (26.2x), lifted 7.5% for the pharma sector's five-year move, gives **28x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹976 cr plus net cash = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY**. Cross-checks: P/E ₹569; DCF ₹303, below the price. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The franchise is bigger than Librela
arguments.p: About 400 clients incl. 16 of the top 20 pharma; BMS renewed to 2035; 5,778 scientists; US FDA/EMA/PMDA-approved sites; ex-Librela revenue grew in high single digits in FY26 (CFO). Few Indian peers offer integrated biologics.

arguments.h: But the earnings reset is deep and not over
arguments.p: Q1FY27: revenue −16%, operating margin 12%, a loss after severance. Research services also lost price-sensitive clients. Guidance cut twice in six months (Jan-2026, Jul-2026). FY27E EPS ₹5.2 vs ₹13.0 before exceptional items in FY24; ROE ~6%.

arguments.h: The biologics capacity is empty for now
arguments.p: Unit 3 (bought for ₹617 cr, capitalised in Q1FY26) runs clinical batches; Bayview (US$36.5 mn plus fit-out) starts later in FY27 and earns from FY28; the original Bengaluru plant lost its anchor. Depreciation and staff costs arrive before revenue.

arguments.h: The price assumes the reset is permanent
arguments.p: ₹365 is 14.9x our FY28E EBITDA and 16.6x trailing, against a 26.2x forward median since 2021 and 46-55x for Indian CDMO peers. Even at today's multiple, our FY28-29E recovery and the cash build give ~₹420. The DCF (₹303) needs ~11% growth for 15 years to reach the price: the recovery has to happen.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether H2 starts to recover and hedge losses ease.
Bayview (Baltimore) operationalised later in FY27; customer lock-ins after that; revenue from FY28.
Zoetis's FY28 Librela forecast (expected by the end of FY27, per management) and any new commercial biologic for Unit 3.
The new commercial team's first full plan: management promised more visibility "from next quarter".
BIOSECURE: the US list of "biotechnology companies of concern" is due within a year of the Dec-2025 enactment.

sections.title: What Syngene does: research for hire (~65% of revenue) and development and manufacturing (~35%), for ~400 clients, 63% of revenue from the US

blocks.p: Syngene is a CRDMO: a contract research, development and manufacturing organisation. Drug companies pay it to do work they would otherwise do in their own labs and plants. It has two businesses. **Research services** (~65% of FY26 revenue by management's split) are discovery chemistry and biology for innovators, paid per scientist (FTE), per project (fee-for-service) or as **dedicated R&D centres**: ring-fenced buildings run only for one client, the largest being Bristol-Myers Squibb's BBRC in Bengaluru with 700+ scientists, renewed to 2035. Translational and clinical research (bioanalysis, a human pharmacology unit, a first global Phase III trial) is a small, growing part. **CDMO** (~35%) takes molecules from process development to clinical and commercial supply, in small molecules (APIs at Bengaluru and the Mangaluru plant) and large molecules (biologics: antibodies, proteins, ADCs at Bengaluru, the Unit 3 site and, from FY28, Bayview in Baltimore).

blocks.callout: **So what:** this is a people business at heart: staff costs were 32.9% of FY26 revenue, materials only ~25%. Revenue is in dollars (US$419 mn in FY26), costs mostly in rupees, so a weaker rupee helps over time, but Syngene hedges forward and booked ₹61 cr of hedge losses in FY26 and ₹50 cr in Q1FY27 as the rupee fell faster than its hedge rates. Two customers above 10% of revenue made up 37.2% of FY26 sales.

blocks.p: Two things in this history matter for the investor today. First, Biocon has treated Syngene as a source of cash: it sold 5.4% in Sep-2022 (₹1,220 cr), 9.96% in Feb-2023 (~₹2,240 cr at ~₹560 a share, to help fund the Viatris deal) and ~2% in Dec-2024 (₹686 cr). It still owns 52.4%, and with Biocon now owning all of Biocon Biologics and carrying debt, further sales are possible: a supply overhang. Second, Syngene's manufacturing strategy was built around one product. The Zoetis contract (2018) was a 10-year programme with potential of up to US$500 mn; Syngene bought Unit 3 (Dec-2023) and Bayview (Mar-2025) partly to diversify away from it, but "by the time that happened, we had a big drop in the opportunity with the large customer" (Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Q1FY27 call).

sections.title: Industry: outsourcing keeps growing (CRO ~11% a year, biologics CDMO ~13%), but near-term research spending is cautious

blocks.p: The global contract research market was ~US$84 bn in 2024 and is expected to reach ~US$140 bn by 2029 (~11% a year); CDMO ~US$130 bn growing ~8%, within which biologics (large-molecule) CDMO is the fastest at ~13% (Frost & Sullivan, in Syngene's AR). The drivers are durable: a 2024-28 patent cliff and US drug-price pressure push big pharma to cut fixed costs and outsource; new drug types (ADCs, peptides, oligonucleotides, bispecifics; over 40% of clinical pipelines) need specialist capacity; and China+1 makes Indian vendors more relevant. The near term is softer: biotech funding recovered in H2-2025 but reaches CRO revenue with a 6-12 month lag, and clients prefer smaller work packages.

sections.title: Tailwind test: BIOSECURE and China+1 help Indian CRDMOs, but there is no sign yet in Syngene's revenue, which fell 16% in Q1FY27

blocks.p: The BIOSECURE Act became US law in Dec-2025 inside the defence authorisation act. The final text names no company: it relies on the Defense Department's 1260H list and a later list of 'biotechnology companies of concern', with due process and grandfathering of existing contracts, so the near-term effect is gradual (AR26 MD&A p.183). Syngene says enquiry levels and RFPs for non-China CRDMOs have risen (AR26) and that the listing of some Chinese companies helps shift molecules to India (CEO, q1call). In FY26 the Act's delays also held back client spending on research projects (AR26 p.185). We see no sign of it in Syngene's revenue yet: Q1FY27 revenue fell 16%.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** the tailwinds are real at the industry level, but Syngene has to win the business. Its CDMO peers are priced as if they will (Divi's 55.1x, Sai Life 46.4x trailing EV/EBITDA at 30-Sep-2026); Syngene at 16.3x is priced as if it will not.

sections.title: Research services (~65%): the BMS centre is secure to 2035, but discovery has drifted into commodity work and is losing clients on price

blocks.p: Research services earned about ₹2,430 cr in FY26 on management's ~65/35 split. The core is chemistry, with biology, biotherapeutics discovery, DMPK and safety assessment around it, sold to large pharma and to small biotechs. The **dedicated centres** are the stable part: BMS has worked with Syngene since 1998, now with 700+ scientists, and in Jan-2026 extended the collaboration to 2035 with a wider scope (discovery to clinical and manufacturing); management expects it to grow "around US inflation". The **discovery** part is the problem. In the Q1FY27 call the new leadership said Syngene had "drifted towards the larger share of commoditised research services where differentiation is limited, and pricing pressure is inevitable", and that a few clients left on cost. Q1FY27 research revenue was ~₹574 cr (78% of ₹736 cr), roughly −1.5% on our estimate for Q1FY26 despite a much weaker rupee.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the dedicated-centre model (BMS and others) is the best business Syngene has: long contracts, client-funded infrastructure, low churn. Discovery FTE work is not: Indian and Chinese rivals sell chemistry hours more cheaply, and AI tools may reduce the hours needed per programme. Management's plan (AI-led, new modalities, integrated discovery-to-development) is sensible but unproven; we give research services almost no growth in FY27 and less than the market after.

sections.title: CDMO (~35%): Librela, the one large commercial product, has gone to near zero; we cut CDMO revenue 21% in FY27E and assume no replacement of similar size

blocks.p: The CDMO business was about ₹1,309 cr in FY26. Its largest piece was commercial manufacture of bedinvetmab, the antibody in **Librela** (Zoetis's monthly injection for osteoarthritis pain in dogs). Syngene signed the long-term Zoetis contract in 2018: a 10-year programme with potential of up to US$500 mn (CFO, Q3FY26 call), whose early years ran above the average as Zoetis filled its distribution channels. From the start of FY26 Zoetis cut orders to run down inventory, and the CFO also pointed to a "product issue" in public reports on the drug. Syngene cut its FY26 guidance in Jan-2026 to a 3-5% constant-currency decline because Librela volumes were slower than expected. In Q1FY27 there was "almost no Librela"; management sizes the impact at "nearly $50 million" a year, says Zoetis holds inventory for "the next couple of years", has only small delivery obligations in H2FY27, and does not expect volumes to be zero in FY28. Syngene has no commercial role in Zoetis's follow-on antibody Lenivia.

Utilisation of the biologics network is the single biggest swing factor in FY28-29 margins. We assume Bayview and Unit 3 earn clinical and some commercial revenue from FY28 (CDMO +16-17%), not a Librela-sized contract.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: real in scale, the BMS model and regulatory record; weak in discovery pricing; the biologics edge is unproven without an anchor client

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. Syngene used to show one: ROE of 16-20% in FY19-21 on a net-cash balance sheet. It no longer does: ROE fell to 11% in FY25 and 6.6% in FY26, below a ~12% cost of equity. Part of that is cyclical (Librela, empty new plants), but part is structural: management itself says discovery has become commoditised. What remains durable is scale, the dedicated-centre model, and a clean regulatory record. Rivals for the same work include Sai Life, Aragen, Anthem, Jubilant Biosys and Piramal in India, and WuXi, Pharmaron and Samsung Biologics abroad.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** a narrow moat, narrower than three years ago. The BMS centre and the quality record are real advantages. Discovery FTE work has little pricing power, and the biologics manufacturing edge only becomes a moat if Syngene can win and keep commercial products other than Librela. We would not pay a premium for durability today; the target multiple is Syngene's own history, not a premium to it.

sections.title: Q4 is always the strongest quarter and Q1 the weakest; Q1FY27 (₹736 cr, 12% margin) was the worst quarter in four years

blocks.p: Customer advances arrive in January-March and many contracts close at the fiscal year-end, so Q4 is Syngene's biggest quarter (₹1,018 cr in Q4FY25, ₹1,036 cr in Q4FY26, with 29-34% margins) and Q1 its smallest. In Q1FY27 revenue fell 16% to ₹736 cr with almost no Librela; the operating margin fell to 12.4% (Screener) after a ₹50 cr forex hedge loss, and the company made a ₹9 cr loss after a ₹10 cr severance charge. Management guides to an H2 that is "much stronger" than H1.

sections.title: Revenue doubled in seven years at a ~30% margin; then FY26 stalled (+3%), the margin fell to 25% and profit before exceptional items fell 20%

blocks.p: Syngene grew revenue from ₹1,826 cr in FY19 to ₹3,739 cr in FY26, ~11% a year, while holding an EBITDA margin of 29-31% (Screener basis, which is the company's 'operating EBITDA': forex hedge results inside, other income outside). Growth came in two legs: discovery and dedicated centres for big pharma (BMS above all), and commercial biologics manufacturing for Zoetis's dog-arthritis antibody Librela under a 2018 long-term contract. That second leg has now gone into reverse. FY25 revenue grew only 4%, FY26 3% (US$ revenue fell from US$430 mn to US$419 mn), and in FY26 the margin dropped to 24.6%: Librela volumes fell, the newly capitalised Unit 3 biologics plant added cost without much revenue, staff costs rose 14%, and hedges booked at ~₹87/$ lost money as the rupee fell (₹61 cr). Profit before exceptional items fell from ₹475 cr to ₹380 cr; reported profit from ₹496 cr to ₹317 cr after labour-code and severance charges.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** FY26 was not a one-quarter wobble. Underlying (ex-Librela) growth was 'high single digits' in constant currency (CFO), but that was before Q1FY27, when revenue fell 16% and research services also lost clients. We forecast EPS of ₹5.2 / 8.6 / 11.3 for FY27-29E: FY27 is the trough, and FY29 only gets back to FY23's EPS. Operating cash flow stays healthy (₹915 cr in FY26) and the balance sheet is net cash, so this is an earnings problem, not a solvency one.

sections.title: Margins: 28-31% for six years, 24.6% in FY26, 12.4% in Q1FY27; we forecast 20.0% / 23.5% / 25.0%, below the mid-20s guide for FY27

blocks.p: Syngene's margin (Screener basis = company operating EBITDA) held at 28-31% from FY19 to FY25. In FY26 it fell to 24.6% and in Q1FY27 to 12.4%. Four things did it: (1) lost Librela volume on a fixed-cost biologics base; (2) staff costs up 14% in FY26 to 32.9% of revenue, before cost cuts and severance (₹33 cr pre-tax in FY26, ₹13 cr in Q1FY27, booked as exceptional); (3) Unit 3 capitalised in Q1FY26, adding costs and depreciation; (4) forex hedge losses (₹61 cr in FY26, ₹50 cr in Q1FY27, i.e. 1.6 and 6.8 points of revenue) because forward contracts were struck at ~₹87/$ while the rupee fell past ₹89-95. Material costs are low and stable (~24-25% of revenue).

sections.title: Valuation: 28x Sep-28E EBITDA gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}, BUY); the market pays 14.9x FY28E, and the DCF says the price already needs ~11% growth

blocks.p: The brokers that disclose a method value Syngene on **EV/EBITDA**: ICICI Securities (24x FY27E EBITDA in its last accessible note), Nuvama (22x inside its Biocon sum of the parts) and YES Securities (EV/EBITDA in its valuation table). Macquarie, Jefferies, Goldman Sachs and Kotak targets came without a method in the material we could read; none stated P/E. We follow the street: **EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E EBITDA (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, plus Sep-28E net cash (₹2,210 cr after ₹449 cr of leases, consistent with EBITDA after Ind AS 116 lease costs). EV/EBITDA also suits a trough year better than P/E: FY27E EPS is depressed by depreciation on plants that do not yet earn. P/E and a DCF are cross-checks.

We use Syngene's one-year-forward EV/EBITDA **since 1-Apr-2021**, on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (288 points): price × shares then outstanding, less the net cash (incl. leases) last published at the March year-end, divided by the next full fiscal year's EBITDA (actual FY23-26; our FY27E for Apr-2025 to Mar-2026 and FY28E for Apr-Sep 2026). EBITDA is before exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same. **Trough test on EBITDA:** a forward year is left out if its EBITDA is negative or below half the best of the three years before; FY27E (₹695 cr) is above half of FY25's ₹1,045 cr, so no year is excluded (none). We multiply the median by the nine pharma peers' five-year EV/EBITDA move (+7.5%; Syngene is outside the set) and round to the nearest half-turn. Syngene's own de-rating and growth do not enter the base; they are sensitivities below.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a damaged but solvent franchise priced for no recovery; on the house method we initiate with BUY, and the case stands or falls on FY28 growth

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** one of India's largest integrated CRDMOs: ~400 clients, 16 of the top 20 pharma companies, BMS's 700-scientist dedicated centre (India's first and largest) renewed to 2035, 5,778 scientists, biologics plants in India and the US that few Indian peers have, and ₹1,800 cr of net cash. **What you are not buying:** a growth company today. Revenue falls in FY27, ROE is ~6%, discovery is losing price-sensitive clients, the biologics plants lost their one large commercial product, and the CEO has changed twice in 18 months.

**What you are paying:** ₹365 is 14.9x our FY28E EBITDA (16.6x trailing) and 42.7x our FY28E EPS. On the street's method (EV/EBITDA), Syngene's own 26.2x median since 2021 lifted by the sector's +7.5% gives 28x Sep-28E EBITDA = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a BUY under the house rule. The P/E cross-check (₹569) is lower but also well above the price; the DCF (₹303) is below it. In plain words: the stock is cheap against its own history and its peers, and not cheap against a DCF. Most of the upside to our target is the re-rating; without any, the FY28-29 recovery and the cash build alone give ~₹420. Both need the recovery to happen.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Syngene International (consolidated, Rs crore). Syngene reports one segment (contract research and manufacturing) and discloses only the share of research services vs CDMO; the engine runs one revenue-growth path and the two-line build sits in businessLines, checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/SYNGENE.ctx.js. EBITDA on Screener's basis = the company's 'operating EBITDA' (excludes other income, includes forex hedge gains/losses). Other income and interest are built in SYNGENE.ctx.js from sourced parts and written here by SYNGENE.mult.js. Valued on EV/EBITDA, the method the brokers that disclose one use.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the two-line build below. FY27 -7.0%: Q1FY27 revenue -16% (Rs736 cr) on no Zoetis offtake and attrition of a few research clients; guidance is a single-digit rupee decline ('mid-single-digit', CFO, 30-Jul-2026) with H2 stronger than H1. Our -7% needs Q2-Q4 revenue of ~Rs2,740 cr, -4% on last year's Rs2,864 cr; we sit a little below the guide because guidance was cut in Jan-2026 (FY26) and again in Jul-2026 (FY27). FY28 +9.7% and FY29 +10.8%: Librela is out of the base, Bayview (US) starts earning in FY28, Mangaluru and Unit 3 fill, and the BMS centre grows with US inflation; management aims for double-digit growth from FY28 but gave no number. Rupee: FY26 ~Rs89/$ (US$419 mn), ~Rs94-95/$ in Q1FY27; we assume no further move after FY27.

base._why: FY26 revenue Rs3,738.7 cr split ~65/35 between research services (discovery, dedicated R&D centres, translational & clinical) and CDMO (small- and large-molecule development and manufacturing): 'two-thirds, one-third... around 65, 35' (CFO, Q3FY26 call), 41% CDMO in Q4FY26 (CEO, Q4 call). Company does not disclose rupee figures; this split is ours.

businessLines._why: Research +0.5% in FY27: Q1 research ~Rs574 cr (78% of Rs736 cr) vs ~Rs583 cr a year earlier (two-thirds of Rs874 cr), i.e. ~-1.5%, after losing commoditised clients on price; the rupee (~+6%) and the BMS extension to 2035 hold it flat for the year. +7% / +8% in FY28-29 as biotech funding recovers (6-12 month lag) and the AI/new-modality offering is sold; still below the 11% market growth. CDMO -21% in FY27: Librela (~US$50 mn in FY26 by our estimate from 'impact nearly $50 million', q1call) falls to minor late-year deliveries; Q1 CDMO ~Rs162 cr (22%) vs ~Rs291 cr; ex-Librela CDMO grows ~13% on Mangaluru lock-ins and Unit 3 clinical batches. +16% / +17% in FY28-29: Bayview contracts (one or two converted), Mangaluru and Unit 3 ramp from a low base; no large commercial biologic replaces Librela in our base case.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis = company operating EBITDA (incl. forex hedge results, ex other income): 28.6% FY25, 24.6% FY26 (incl. a Rs61 cr hedge loss), 12.3% Q1FY27 (incl. a Rs50 cr hedge loss; 19% without it). Guidance: 'mid-20s' for FY27, which needs ~29% in Q2-Q4 against 25% a year earlier when Librela was still shipping. We take 20.0%: Q2-Q4 at ~22.7%, with the rupee still well above the hedge rates (Q3FY26 hedged at ~Rs86.9 vs spot ~Rs89.4), staff costs at ~33% of revenue and the empty biologics capacity (Unit 3 capitalised from Q1FY26), offset by FY26-27 cost cuts. FY28 23.5%: hedge losses fade, revenue grows, but Bayview is capitalised and its costs enter the P&L before it fills. FY29 25.0%: utilisation; still below the 28-30% of FY23-25.
assumptions._capexWhy: Screener capex (CFO less FCF): Rs489 cr FY24, Rs770 cr FY25 (incl. Bayview, US$36.5 mn), Rs368 cr FY26 (~US$45 mn guided). Q1FY27 Rs70 cr, mostly Bayview and technology/AI. No FY27 number guided; we assume Rs400 cr (Bayview operationalisation, capability labs, maintenance), Rs450 cr and Rs500 cr as growth returns; Rs1,040 cr of CWIP at Mar-26 (Bayview and others) is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs453 cr (incl. Rs42 cr on right-of-use assets) on Screener's gross block; Q1FY27 Rs112 cr (Rs448 cr a year). Bayview (~Rs410 cr in CWIP incl. land and pre-operating cost) is not capitalised in FY27 (CEO, q1call) and adds ~Rs25-30 cr a year from FY28. The rate is set so depreciation runs ~Rs465 / 490 / 520 cr in FY27-29E (see SYNGENE.ctx.js output).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury income is built in SYNGENE.ctx.js on gross cash, deposits, ICDs and liquid funds (engine net cash + leases + borrowings) and entered in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (checked in SYNGENE.ctx.js): (1) treasury income at 4.27%, the yield Syngene realised in FY26 (interest on deposits and ICDs Rs59.1 cr + gains on liquid funds Rs9.4 cr on average year-end gross treasury of ~Rs1,605 cr: Rs1,399 cr at Mar-25, Rs1,810 cr at Mar-26), applied to average gross treasury (engine net cash + Rs449 cr of leases + Rs9.4 cr of bank debt - Rs39.7 cr of strategic unlisted stakes): Rs1,810 -> 1,990 -> 2,383 -> 2,876 cr, Mar-26 to Mar-29E; (2) interest on lease and security deposits ~Rs1 cr (FY26 Rs1.1 cr). Tax-refund interest (FY26 Rs1.1 cr, FY25 Rs4.7 cr) is not repeated; forex sits in EBITDA. FY26 company other income Rs70.7 cr; Q1FY27 Rs25 cr; twelve months to Jun-26 ~Rs79 cr. Screener's history nets exceptional items (FY26 -Rs9 cr).

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits with maturity of more than 12 months (Rs275.4 cr at Mar-26, Rs1.8 cr at Mar-25) sit in non-current other financial assets (AR26 note 6(a)), inside Screener's Other Assets; they are treasury. With them, net cash excluding leases equals the company's Rs1,800 cr.

assumptions._interestWhy: Built in SYNGENE.ctx.js: lease interest at FY26's 8.4% (Rs38.2 cr on average leases of ~Rs454 cr) on Rs449 cr of lease liabilities held flat (Rs37.8 cr) + 10% on Rs9.4 cr of short-term bank debt + ~Rs1.5 cr of exchange differences and other finance costs (FY26 Rs4.0 cr as packing-credit debt fell from Rs120 cr). FY26 finance cost Rs48.8 cr (borrowings Rs6.6 cr, leases Rs38.2 cr, exchange difference Rs4.0 cr); Q1FY27 Rs10 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 normalised 22.1% (Rs108 cr on pre-exceptional PBT of Rs488 cr); FY26 guide 21-23%; Q4FY26 24.2% as profit shifts across units; MAT credit of Rs95 cr left at Mar-26 (AR26 note 7). 23% in FY27, 24% after as SEZ benefits run off.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend of Rs1.25 a share for FY25 and FY26 (~Rs50 cr); we keep ~Rs1.25-1.40 a share: 25% of FY27E EPS, 15% / 13% after.

dcf._betaWhy: Beta 0.95 (12.2% cost of equity). Net cash, so WACC equals the cost of equity; earnings have proved more volatile than a contract-research model suggests (Librela).
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%, mid-range of the house 5-6%: outsourcing keeps growing (CRO market ~11% a year to 2029) but Syngene's research arm is losing price-sensitive work.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Growth fades from ~11% (FY29E) to 7% by FY42E; Syngene grew revenue ~11% a year in FY19-26 (Rs1,826 cr to Rs3,739 cr).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 26%: back towards the mid-20s guided as normal, below the 29-31% of FY19-25 when Librela carried the biologics plants.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex ~11-12% of sales in FY27-29E fades to 10% (maintenance ~9% of sales plus growth capex at Syngene's ~0.8x gross asset turn).
dcf._wcNote: Operating working capital is negative (~-16% of FY26 sales on Screener's balance sheet) because customers pay advances (Rs664 cr) and fund some assets (deferred revenue); the engine holds it at that level, so falling revenue in FY27 costs cash.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The new commercial team wins a commercial biologic for Unit 3 or Bayview, Zoetis orders more Librela for FY28, BIOSECURE moves China-sourced molecules to India and discovery pricing firms; growth runs ~3 points a year faster and margins return to the high 20s.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Discovery keeps losing price-sensitive clients, Bayview stays empty after capitalisation and hedge losses persist; growth runs ~4 points a year slower and margins stay near FY27's ~20%.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Syngene: the brokers that disclose a method use EV/EBITDA (ICICI Securities 24x FY27E in its last accessible note, Apr-2025; Nuvama values Syngene at 22x EV/EBITDA inside its Biocon sum of the parts, Nov-2025; YES Securities shows EV/EBITDA in its valuation table); Macquarie, Jefferies, Goldman Sachs and Kotak targets come without a method. 28x = Syngene's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Apr-2021 (every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 288 points; EV = price x shares then outstanding less the net cash last published at the March year-end, incl. leases; forward EBITDA = the next full year's: actual FY23-26, our FY27E/FY28E; EBITDA is before exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same; no trough year: FY27E EBITDA is above half the FY24-26 peak) of 26.2x x 1.075 (the nine pharma peers' EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians; Syngene is outside the set, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +7.5%) = 28.2x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net cash. Bull 34.5x / bear 24.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (31.9x / 23.0x) x 1.075. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by SYNGENE.mult.js.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check: Syngene's median one-year-forward P/E since 1-Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items (same weekly closes; FY27 left out as a trough year: FY27E EPS Rs5.22 is below half of FY24's Rs12.96) of 53.0x x 1.082 (nine peers' five-year P/E move, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +8.2%) = 57.3x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EPS. Reported-EPS median 53.6x (sensitivity). Bull 72.5x / bear 51x = 75th / 25th percentile x 1.082.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 12.2% (cost of equity; net cash), terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash at Mar-27.
